facts.uncertainty: ~1% by cross-validation. TWO CORRECTIONS BEHIND THIS NUMBER, both caught before it was published. (1) A first pass read every cached ratio 2x high by assuming the cache was uint16 in [N, seq+1] rows; it is a FLAT torch.int32 token tensor (tokens_cot.pt: shape (424056227,), element_size 4). Cross-validation exposed it as a clean 49.62%/50.38% error, and a tidy factor of two on two domains three orders of magnitude apart is a wrong constant, not sampling noise. (2) A second pass sampled the FIRST 1000 rows; uniform sampling moved this domain +38.1% and chat_qa +39.6%, while cot moved +0.2% and zh_web -0.4%. The chat shards are ordered and the head is not the file -- and because the two cross-validation domains are homogeneous, cross-validation could NOT have caught this one. 6e named it before the measurement.

facts.value: Of the nine domains data/mix_500m.json names, FIVE have less supply than it demands and already run on epoch repetition: chatml 0.294x, chat_qa 0.296x, cot 0.263x, en_c4_stage2 0.738x, textbook_30b 0.792x. FOUR have surplus: zh_web 34.91x, code_py_starcoder 1.332x, code_py_rp1t 1.331x, math_owm_stage2 1.235x. Demand is rows x weight summed over both phases, equal to rows x weight to four decimals here because every domain's anneal weight equals its weight. CONSEQUENCE FOR A CACHE TRUNCATION (de-2): capping a cache at the schedule's own row count binds on the four surplus domains and cannot bind on the five deficit ones, so no domain's distinct-document count changes. Recoverable bytes are 96.9 GB of 165.9 GB, of which zh_web alone is 85 GB. THE EPOCH FIELD IS A CAP, NOT A MULTIPLIER: `want` at train.py:1754 comes from the token budget and never from len(pool), and `epochs` appears only in the cap that binds when len(pool)*epochs < demand.

facts.value: Text bytes per token under the frozen data/tokenizer.json, from uniform 1000-row samples -- HIGHER IS BETTER COMPRESSION: zh_web 4.216, chatml 3.739, chat_qa 3.607, cot 2.828. So cot is the domain the vocabulary handles WORST, at 2.83 bytes per token, and it is English mathematical chain-of-thought against a vocabulary fitted on Chinese web plus cosmopedia -- which is the direction unfreeze condition 2 predicts. The two chat domains sit between cot and zh_web, 11-14% below Chinese web rather than above it.

facts.value: 49 corpus domains, 3,760 shards. PROVENANCE IS TIERED BY BUILD DATE, not by domain: 14 carry filters_fp (the content hash of the filters/*.py that produced them) and are rebuildable; 30 carry only a content fingerprint, so a changed byte is detectable but WHICH filter code produced them is unrecoverable; 5 carry no build_corpus_stats.json at all (code_rp1t_rest, cot_seed, web_cci3_p0/p22/p23). SIZE HAS TWO ANSWERS AND THEY DIFFER BY 40%: disk usage is 248.93 GB, the sum of file sizes is 348.30 GB, and the gap is 2,010 files with link count > 1 -- hardlinked shards under two domain names. Consequences: deleting one of a hardlinked pair frees nothing, and a write through either name changes both.
